messages:
eva: Heads-up — saw a latency spike on staging around 10:12 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~900ms, throughput down ~30%. KV cache miss rate looks higher but traces are sparse. anyone oncall?

mike: i'm on. can you paste links / quick metrics?

eva: https://grafana.internal/redwood/staging-runtime p95+throughput panels. prometheus shows kvcache_miss_rate ~0.32 at 10:11-10:14.

sarika: i only see heartbeat events in traces. jaeger sampler for runtime shows 0.05 during that window — super low. nothing after 10:11 in spans. did someone change sampler config?

obs-bot: Alert: latency-surge detected for service=runtime-staging at 2026-11-03T10:12:07Z

jonathan: checked batcher logs around 10:11:43 — observed a wave of kernel fallbacks to generic kernel for a subset of requests. snippet: 
```
[10:11:43] batcher: kernel_pick=optimized_avx failed->fallback=generic
[10:11:43] reason=kernel_checksum_mismatch
```

mike: fallback correlates with a spike in long sequences from a tiny set of clients. seqlen histogram shifted right briefly. maybe the kernel fingerprinting misclassified a canary model variant.

sarika: kvcache shows a burst of evictions and prefetch retries. logs: 
```
kvcache.evictions: 412
prefetch.retries: 78
```
that should have raised the dashboard but the evictions panel is flat in grafana for that window.

eva: exactly — prometheus scrape has the evictions series, but our grafana rollup/derived metric for "eviction_rate_5m" has a hole between 10:10-10:15 (scrape job missed). so dashboard mismatches the raw metrics.

jonathan: looks like trace density low because a recent canary deployment set RUNTIME_TRACE_SAMPLE=0.05 in the env. canary was rolled at 10:05. that would explain the missing spans.

mike: where did that env var come from? release config shows a change in deployment template in PR #2345 (dataplane-rollout). could be accidental.

sarika: also saw a regression in kernel selection heuristics in that same deploy — simplified heuristic now only checks model arch string: 
```
if (model.arch == "gpt") fast_path = true;
```
which ignores kv cache warmness and seq_len. that explains forced fast-path picks then sudden fallbacks when seq_len spiked.

mike: yikes. that's a regression candidate. revert heuristic until we add more signals.

eva: short-term mitigation plan: 1) pin kernel selection to previous stable mapping for canary and prod, 2) bump tracer sampler default to 0.2 for staging to regain span density, 3) increase prefetch worker concurrency +2 to reduce retries. i'll start rollback now.

jonathan: also add a temporary metric export for kernel_fallback_rate with no sampling — current metric is sampled at 10% and the spike got dropped.

obs-bot: Deploy (rollback kernel heuristic) started by eva at 2026-11-03T10:28:14Z

mike: after rollback p95 back to ~130ms by 10:36. throughput normalized. traces still thin but better after sampler bump.

sarika: follow-ups (to file): - fix batching heuristic to consider kv_cache_hit_rate and seqlen histogram; - make prefetch OOM/backoff visible in dashboards; - change tracer config so sampler is per-deployment flag, not canary-only; - ensure derived grafana rollups tolerate short scrape gaps.

eva: i've created tickets: TICKET-789 (batching heuristics + kv signals), TICKET-790 (tracing sampler default & env guard), TICKET-791 (dashboard rollup resilience). assigning to runtime+infra.

jonathan: pls add a unit/integration test for kernel_pick that feeds synthetic seq_len distributions and kv warmness to avoid regressions.

mike: thanks folks :thumbsup:
